record.original_question: Can one design a general framework for combining constraint-solving algorithms, including algorithms for unification, equations and disequations, shared constants or constructors, membership constraints, and non-free solution domains?

evidence.quote: Design a framework for combining constraint solving algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Constraint solving in symbolic computation encompasses a wide variety of procedures, including:

- syntactic and equational unification algorithms (computing solutions to equations s = t modulo a given equational theory E),
- algorithms for systems of equations together with disequations (disunification),
- algorithms over signatures whose theories share certain symbols, such as shared constants or shared free constructors,
- algorithms handling membership constraints (e.g., sort or regular-tree constraints requiring variables to range over specified sets), and
- algorithms over non-free solution domains (algebraic structures that are not initial/free in the corresponding theory).

Each of these classes admits its own combination results (for instance, decision procedures for unifiability in disjoint equational theories can be combined under suitable conditions, and analogous methods exist for disunification with linear constant restrictions).

Problem. Design a single general framework for combining constraint-solving algorithms that simultaneously encompasses all of the above settings. More precisely, formulate a uniform notion of "constraint solver" and a uniform combination procedure such that, given constraint solvers S_1, …, S_n for theories (or constraint languages) L_1, …, L_n satisfying explicitly stated abstract hypotheses, the framework produces a constraint solver for the combined constraint language L_1 ∪ … ∪ L_n, and such that the existing combination results for unification, for equations-plus-disequations, for theories sharing constants or constructors, for membership constraints, and for constraint solving over non-free domains all arise as instances of this single framework.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as RTA open problem #43 (originator Jean-Pierre Jouannaud) and remains an active research direction. Substantial partial progress exists: combination methods for unification in disjoint equational theories, extensions to disunification with linear constant restrictions, combination of solvers over algebraic domains sharing constants, and uniform treatments of non-equality predicates have been developed. However, no single unifying framework covering all listed cases (unification, disequations, shared constants/constructors, membership constraints, and non-free domains) has been established, so the problem is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: RTA Problem #43
status_evidence.snippet: Design a framework for combining constraint solving algorithms. Originator: Jean-Pierre Jouannaud.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as an open problem in the RTA list of open problems in rewriting.

status_evidence.title: Combining Symbolic Constraint Solvers on Algebraic Domains
status_evidence.snippet: Combining constraint solvers on different algebraic domains that may share some constant symbols, extending techniques from combining unification in disjoint equational theories.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: combination methods for solvers over algebraic domains sharing constants are known.

status_evidence.title: Combination techniques and decision problems for disunification
status_evidence.snippet: Method to combine decision procedures for unifiability in disjoint equational theories, with variants applicable to disunification.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the disunification case via linear constant restrictions.
